verses.text: When the seventh month came, the Israelites were living in their towns. Then all the people gathered together in Jerusalem as one.

Jeshua son of Jozadak and his fellow priests, and Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel and his relatives, began to build the altar of the God of Israel. They wanted to offer burnt offerings on it, as written in the law of Moses, the man of God.
They were afraid of the people living in the lands around them, but they still built the altar on its old base. They offered burnt offerings on it to the LORD every morning and evening.
They celebrated the Festival of Shelters as the law says. Each day they offered the number of burnt offerings required for that day.
After that they offered the regular burnt offerings, the offerings for the New Moon festivals, and for all the LORD's holy festivals. They also offered the gifts people chose to give to the LORD.
They began offering burnt offerings to the LORD on the first day of the seventh month, even though the foundation of the LORD's temple had not yet been laid.

They gave money to the stoneworkers and carpenters. They gave food, drink, and olive oil to the people of Sidon and Tyre, so they would bring cedar logs by sea from Lebanon to Joppa. King Cyrus of Persia had given them permission for this.

In the second month of the second year after they arrived at God's temple site in Jerusalem, the work began. Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, Jeshua son of Jozadak, the rest of their fellow priests and Levites, and all who had come back to Jerusalem from being prisoners started the work. They chose Levites twenty years old and older to be in charge of the work on the LORD's temple.

Jeshua with his sons and relatives, and Kadmiel and his sons, descendants of Judah, joined together to be in charge of the workers on God's temple. The sons of Henadad and their sons and relatives, who were Levites, helped them.

When the builders laid the foundation of the LORD's temple, the priests stood in their robes with trumpets, and the Levites, the descendants of Asaph, stood with cymbals. They praised the LORD, as David king of Israel had directed.

They sang back and forth to each other, praising and thanking the LORD: "He is good. His love for Israel lasts forever." All the people gave a great shout of praise to the LORD, because the foundation of the LORD's temple had been laid.
But many of the older priests, Levites, and family leaders who had seen the first temple cried out loud when they saw the foundation of this temple being laid. Many others shouted for joy.
No one could tell the difference between the shouts of joy and the sound of crying, because the people made so much noise. The sound was heard far away.
